record.original_question: Does Hilb_d(A^3) have an irreducible component of dimension smaller than 3d, or does the punctual Hilbert scheme Hilb_d(A^3, 0) have an irreducible component of dimension smaller than 2(d - 1)?

evidence.quote: Problem IV. Does there exist a component of Hilbd(A^3) of dimension smaller than 3d? Does there exist a component of Hilbd(A^3, 0) of dimension smaller than 2(d - 1)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, and let $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^3)$ denote the Hilbert scheme parameterizing zero-dimensional closed subschemes of length $d$ in affine three-space $\mathbb{A}^3_k$. Let $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^3, 0) \subset \mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^3)$ denote the punctual Hilbert scheme, parameterizing those subschemes whose support is the origin $0 \in \mathbb{A}^3$.

It is known that the smoothable component of $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^3)$ has dimension $3d$, and that the punctual smoothable component of $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^3, 0)$ has dimension $2(d-1)$ (for $d \geq 1$).

Determine whether either of the following holds:
(a) There exists a positive integer $d$ such that $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^3)$ has an irreducible component of dimension strictly less than $3d$.
(b) There exists a positive integer $d$ such that $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^3, 0)$ has an irreducible component of dimension strictly less than $2(d-1)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerning whether the Hilbert scheme of points on affine 3-space can have a component of dimension below the expected 3d (or 2(d-1) in the punctual case) is listed among the open problems on components of Hilbert schemes; the AIM problem list and recent surveys reference it without resolution. Known results produce components of larger-than-expected dimension (e.g. an (8d-7)-dimensional component for d≥4), and irreducibility is established only for small d, but no smaller-than-expected component has been constructed.

status_evidence.claim: No known elementary components of Hilb_d(A^3) have dimension less than 3d.
